subject: Is there a zero inflation problem with mark recapture models?

messages.author: e9d15d3db318631b
messages.subject: Is there a zero inflation problem with mark recapture models?
parts:
I'm wondering if it could be a problem for a CJS model when you have a lot of individuals that were seen only once and never seen again (e.g. 001000 or 100000 etc. vs 110000 or 001110 etc.)

if you have 1300 lines in your capture history where an individual has been seen only once compared to >2 times have only 500 lines, is it biasing your survival or recapture rate estimates? 

Is it possible to delete all the 1300 lines containing only one capture and no recapture?

messages.author: 312eda23f89ab6c6
messages.subject: AW: Is there a zero inflation problem with mark recapture models?
parts: It’s possible that there are transients in the data (individuals that are present in the study area only at one occasion) or that survival has an age structure with juvenile survival being lower than adult survival. Classical goodness-of-fit test as can be done in U-CARE are indicative about these potential problems. Models exist that can account for transients or that have an age structure (see e.g. the paper by Roger Pradel (1997) in Biometrics). Deleting the capture histories of all individual captured only once is wrong and would result in a positive bias of the estimate of survival.

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: Is there a zero inflation problem with mark recapture models?
parts:
[sending now to the whole list]

this could be a problem of transience  which can be dealt with using a zero-inflation type of a model.  There are quite a few papers on modeling transience, I think some of them are cited in the Royle and Dorazio (2008) book around p 363. I think Pradel et al. (1997) and Hines et al. (2003).   The basic idea is you introduce a latent parameter R_{I} = 1 if resident 0 otherwise and R_{I} ~ Bern(theta) or something, and then the CJS model applies to the R_{I} = 1 individuals.
I imagine Kery and Schaub talk about this in the BPA book too or cite some references but I can't remember.
regards
andy

messages.author: e9d15d3db318631b
messages.subject: Re: Is there a zero inflation problem with mark recapture models?
parts:
Hello, 

Thanks for your help! So it can definitively make the estimation of survival difficult. Especially when the recapture rates are low (~20%, which is my case). 

I ran this: 

library(R2ucare)
overall_CJS(data$X, rep(1,nrow(data$X)), rounding = 300)

data$X is the capture history 
rep(1,nrow(data$X)): is the vector of the # of individuals per line (only 1 individual per line in the capture history). 

And got that: 

                           chi2 degree_of_freedom p_value
Gof test for CJS model: 140.655                38       1.059153e-13

It seems to me that there are 2 types of GOF. Using the dipper example (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/R2ucare/R2ucare.pdf), which is exactly the way my data is structured, I found p.val = 0. But there is also the model comparison where you compare the data you have with the data estimated by the model... 

Does that mean that CJS is not a good model for the data I have?
